nodes.name: Ni nanocones electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Electrodeposition of NiNCs was performed in a two-electrode cell configuration in which a piece of Ni foam (1×1 cm²) served as a positive electrode, and a platinum plate was used as a negative electrode. The electrosynthesis solution comprised NiCl2·6H2O (1.0 M), NH4Cl (3.0 M), and ammonia (NH3·H2O 25%) (2.0 M). Electrosynthesis of NiNCs was performed via a constant current method by applying a current of 60 mA cm⁻² for 10 min at 60°C. Finally, the NiNCs-decorated Ni foam (≈0.31 mm) was thoroughly rinsed with doubly distilled water and dried at 60°C for 6 h (Figure S1a, Supporting Information).

nodes.name: Ni-Co-Fe LDH electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The Ni-Co-Fe LDH was prepared according to our previous study. Briefly, the Ni-Co-Fe LDH was electrosynthesized in a three-electrode cell setup comprising a NiNCs-decorated Ni foam (1×1 cm²) as a working electrode, a platinum plate counter electrode, and an Ag/AgCl reference electrode. The LDH film was electrosynthesized from a solution containing Co(NO3)2·6H2O (11.2×10⁻³ M), Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (11.2×10⁻³ M) and Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (7.5×10⁻³ M) as well as KNO3 (30.0×10⁻³ M) as the supporting electrolyte by consecutive potential sweeping (from -0.7 to -1.2 V vs Ag/AgCl) at a scan rate of 50 mV s⁻¹ (Figure S1b, Supporting Information). Note that electrosynthesis of an LDH film on a bare Ni foam requires ≈16 CV cycles whereas that on a NiNCs-decorated Ni foam requires only 4 to 6 CV cycles. The molar ratio of MII:MIII was 3:1, and the molarity of KNO3 was equal to the sum of the molarities of the MII (CoII and NiII) and MIII (FeIII) species (the optimized Ni:Co:Fe ratio was 1.5:1.5:1). Optimizations of the electrosynthesis condition for the best catalytic performances are presented in the Supporting Information (Figures S2 and S3, Supporting Information). Finally, the Ni-Co-Fe LDH electrodeposited on NiNCs (LDH@NiNC) film was washed with doubly distilled water and dried at 60°C for 3 h.

nodes.name: TMB electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The TMB was electrosynthesized according to the methods reported previously with a slight modification. The TMB was electrosynthesized in a three-electrode cell configuration comprising the LDH@NiNC electrode (1×1 cm²) as a working electrode, a platinum plate counter electrode, and an Ag/AgCl reference electrode. The electrosynthesis process was conducted by applying a constant potential of 1.1 V (vs Ag/AgCl) for 15 min in a solution containing K2B4O7·4H2O (KB, 0.1 M). Optimizations of the TMB electrosynthesis conditions are presented in the Supporting Information, Figure S4 (Supporting Information). Then, the TMB@NiNC electrode (0.36 mm) was washed with doubly distilled water and dried at 60°C for 3 h (Figure S1c, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: FE-SEM shows NiNCs forming cypress-like structure and TMB@NiNC inheriting vertically aligned nanoplatelet morphology from LDH@NiNC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a shows the field emission scanning electron microscope (FE-SEM) image of a NiNCs-decorated Ni foam substrate... Figure 2b displays the FE-SEM image of the LDH@NiNC electrode, and Figure 2c shows the surface morphology of the TMB@NiNC electrode. As can be seen, the TMB@NiNC catalyst inherits the vertically aligned nanoplatelet morphology of the LDH@NiNC.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM images show TMB nanosheet morphology; TEM confirms amorphous nature of TMB catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2d,e show the transmission electron microscope (TEM) images of the scratched-off TMB catalyst that exhibits a well-defined nanosheet morphology. The TEM image of the TMB reveals the amorphous nature of the catalyst (Figure 2f).

properties.description: High-resolution image showing nanostructure with dark contrast features

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED electron diffraction ring pattern confirms the amorphous nature of TMB catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further investigate the crystallographic characteristics of the TMB, selected area electron diffraction (SAED) and the corresponding fast Fourier transform (FFT) patterns of the catalyst were recorded (Figure 2g,h). The electron diffraction ring pattern confirms the amorphous nature of the catalyst.

properties.description: High-contrast grayscale image showing a bright central spot with radial diffraction pattern indicative of selected area electron diffraction (SAED)

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping shows Ni, Co, Fe, O, and B elements uniformly distributed throughout TMB particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2i-j display high spatial resolution elemental mapping images of the TMB obtained via a high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscope (HAADF-STEM) coupled with EDX-mapping. It can be seen that Ni, Co, Fe, O and B elements are uniformly distributed throughout the TMB particles.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS spectra of TMB display strong elemental peaks for Ni, Co, Fe, O, and B confirming homogeneous distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) spectra of the LDH and TMB display strong elemental peaks for Ni, Co, Fe, O, and N (for the LDH), and Ni, Co, Fe, O, and B (for the TMB).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-IR confirms formation of M(BO3) species in TMB.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We also characterized the TMB sample with FT-IR spectroscopy that confirms the formation of M(BO3) species (Figure S7, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: 11B-NMR shows chemical shift of 10.2 ppm agreeing with three-coordinated borate (sp2 hybridized boron) species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: 11B-NMR spectroscopy of the TMB sample also shows a chemical shift of 10.2 ppm that agrees well with the three-coordinated borate (sp2 hybridized boron) species that are not in the rings.

nodes.characterization_summary: TMB shows no obvious crystalline diffraction peaks providing evidence for boronation-induced amorphization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: However, the XRD pattern of the TMB shows no obvious crystalline diffraction peaks, providing evidence for the boronation-induced amorphization of the catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows TMB B 1s at 191.9 eV (B³⁺ in borate); Ni 2p, Co 2p, Fe 2p binding energies positively shift after boronation of LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The core level XPS spectrum of B 1s presents a peak with a binding energy of 191.9 eV, which can be assigned to B³⁺ in borate (BOx or B(OH)₃) (Figure 3i)... the binding energies of Ni 2p, Co 2p and Fe 2p positively shift to higher values after boronation of the LDH sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS quantifies metal contents yielding empirical formula Ni3Co4Fe3B2H14O20 for TMB.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, we quantified the metal contents of the TMB using an inductively coupled plasma mass spectroscopy (ICP-MS)... The empirical formula of the metal borate sample is essentially Ni3Co4Fe3B2H14O20.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV of TMB shows ΔEₚ=0.125 V, Iₚₐ/Iₚₓ=0.97, integrated surface area 14.47 mA⋅V; ECSA calculated as 51.46 cm² for TMB@NiNC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TMB electrode exhibits... better reversibility (ΔEₚ,TMB = 0.125 V,Iₚₐ/Iₚₓ = 0.97) and a significantly higher integrated surface area (14.47 mA⋅V)... the ECSA for TMB@NiNC is 51.46 cm².

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows TMB@NiNC has ESR=0.15 Ω and Rct=1.35 Ω, lower than LDH@NiNC (ESR=0.25 Ω, Rct=1.5 Ω).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TMB@NiNC catalyst provides an equivalent series resistance (ESR) of 0.15 Ω and charge transfer resistance (Rct) of 1.35 Ω that are smaller than those of the LDH@NiNC catalyst (ESR = 0.25 Ω and Rct = 1.5 Ω).
